concepts.title: Force and Its Effects
concepts.definition: A force is a push or a pull on an object that can change its state of motion, direction, or shape.
concepts.key_idea: A force is any push or pull that can change how an object moves or looks.
question_patterns: What is a force?
What are the effects of force on an object?
How can a force change the shape of an object?
Give one example where a force changes the speed of an object.
Can a force change the direction of a moving object? Explain with an example.

solution_steps.explain: Recognise that a force is being applied on the object.
Check whether the object's speed, direction, or shape changes.
Conclude that the force has caused one of the observed changes.

worked_examples.question: What is a force?
worked_examples.solution: A force is a push or a pull that acts on an object.
worked_examples.answer: A force is a push or pull on an object.

worked_examples.question: What are the effects of force on an object?
worked_examples.solution: A force can change the speed, direction, or shape of an object.
worked_examples.answer: Force can change speed, direction, or shape.

worked_examples.question: Give one example where a force changes the shape of an object.
worked_examples.solution: Squeezing a soft ball with the hand changes its shape.
worked_examples.answer: Squeezing a soft ball changes its shape.

concepts.title: Contact and Non-Contact Forces
concepts.definition: Forces are grouped into contact forces, which need touching, and non-contact forces, which act from a distance.
concepts.key_idea: Some forces need direct contact while others act from a distance without touching.
question_patterns: What are contact forces?
What are non-contact forces?
How do contact and non-contact forces differ?
Give one example of a contact force.
Give one example of a non-contact force.

solution_steps.explain: Decide whether the force needs the objects to touch.
If touching is needed it is a contact force; otherwise it is a non-contact force.
Provide a matching example for the chosen type.

worked_examples.question: What are contact forces?
worked_examples.solution: Contact forces act only when objects touch each other, such as pushing a box.
worked_examples.answer: Forces that need touching, like pushing a box.

worked_examples.question: What are non-contact forces?
worked_examples.solution: Non-contact forces act from a distance, such as a magnet pulling iron.
worked_examples.answer: Forces that act from a distance, like a magnet pulling iron.

worked_examples.question: How do contact and non-contact forces differ?
worked_examples.solution: Contact forces need touching while non-contact forces act from a distance.
worked_examples.answer: Contact forces need touch; non-contact forces do not.

concepts.title: Muscular Force
concepts.definition: Muscular force is the force applied by the muscles of humans or animals to push, pull, or lift objects.
concepts.key_idea: Muscular force comes from the muscles of living beings and is a contact force.
question_patterns: What is muscular force?
Why is muscular force called a contact force?
Give one example of muscular force in daily life.
How do animals use muscular force?
What part of the body produces muscular force?

solution_steps.explain: Note that the force comes from muscles of a human or animal.
Confirm that the muscles touch the object, so it is a contact force.
Provide an example such as lifting a bucket with hands.

worked_examples.question: What is muscular force?
worked_examples.solution: It is the force applied by muscles of humans or animals.
worked_examples.answer: Force applied by muscles of humans or animals.

worked_examples.question: Why is muscular force called a contact force?
worked_examples.solution: Because the muscles must touch the object to apply the force.
worked_examples.answer: Because muscles must touch the object.

worked_examples.question: Give one example of muscular force in daily life.
worked_examples.solution: Lifting a school bag with the hands uses muscular force.
worked_examples.answer: Lifting a school bag with the hands.

concepts.title: Frictional Force
concepts.definition: Frictional force is the contact force that opposes the relative motion between two surfaces in contact.
concepts.key_idea: Friction always acts against the direction of motion or attempted motion.
question_patterns: What is frictional force?
In which direction does friction act?
Why does a rolling ball eventually stop?
Give one example where friction is useful.
How can friction be reduced?

solution_steps.explain: Find the two surfaces that are in contact.
Note the direction in which the object moves or tends to move.
Friction acts opposite to the direction of motion.

worked_examples.question: What is frictional force?
worked_examples.solution: It is the force that opposes motion between two surfaces in contact.
worked_examples.answer: The force that opposes motion between touching surfaces.

worked_examples.question: In which direction does friction act?
worked_examples.solution: Friction acts opposite to the direction of motion or attempted motion.
worked_examples.answer: Opposite to the direction of motion.

worked_examples.question: Why does a rolling ball eventually stop?
worked_examples.solution: Friction between the ball and the ground opposes its motion and stops it.
worked_examples.answer: Friction with the ground stops the ball.

concepts.title: Magnetic Force
concepts.definition: Magnetic force is the non-contact force exerted by a magnet on magnetic materials like iron, nickel, and cobalt.
concepts.key_idea: A magnet can attract or repel objects from a distance without touching them.
question_patterns: What is magnetic force?
Why is magnetic force a non-contact force?
Which materials are attracted by a magnet?
Give one example of magnetic force in daily life.
How do like and unlike poles of a magnet interact?

solution_steps.explain: Note that a magnet is producing the force.
Confirm the object is magnetic, such as iron.
The magnet attracts or repels without contact, so it is a non-contact force.

worked_examples.question: What is magnetic force?
worked_examples.solution: It is the force by which a magnet attracts or repels magnetic materials.
worked_examples.answer: The force of a magnet on magnetic materials.

worked_examples.question: Why is magnetic force a non-contact force?
worked_examples.solution: Because a magnet can attract iron from a distance without touching it.
worked_examples.answer: It acts from a distance without touch.

worked_examples.question: Which materials are attracted by a magnet?
worked_examples.solution: Iron, nickel, and cobalt are attracted by a magnet.
worked_examples.answer: Iron, nickel, and cobalt.

concepts.title: Electrostatic Force
concepts.definition: Electrostatic force is the non-contact force exerted by a charged object on other objects, attracting or repelling them.
concepts.key_idea: A charged object can attract or repel other objects from a distance.
question_patterns: What is electrostatic force?
Why is electrostatic force called a non-contact force?
Give one example of electrostatic force in daily life.
How does a charged balloon attract paper bits?
What kind of objects produce electrostatic force?

solution_steps.explain: Note that an object has become electrically charged.
The charged object attracts or repels other light objects.
Since it acts from a distance, it is a non-contact force.

concepts.title: Gravitational Force
concepts.definition: Gravitational force is the non-contact force by which the Earth (and all objects) attract other objects towards their centre.
concepts.key_idea: Gravity pulls every object towards the Earth and is a non-contact force.
question_patterns: What is gravitational force?
Why does an object fall to the ground when released?
Why is gravitational force a non-contact force?
Give one example of gravitational force in daily life.
Does the Moon experience gravitational force from the Earth?

solution_steps.explain: Note that the Earth is pulling the object downward.
Confirm that no touching is needed for gravity to act.
Gravity is a non-contact force acting on all objects.

worked_examples.question: What is gravitational force?
worked_examples.solution: It is the force by which the Earth attracts objects towards its centre.
worked_examples.answer: The force by which the Earth pulls objects down.

worked_examples.solution: Gravitational force pulls the object towards the Earth.
worked_examples.answer: Gravity pulls the object down.

worked_examples.solution: Because the Earth pulls objects even when they are not touching it.
worked_examples.answer: It acts without contact.

concepts.title: Effects of Force on Motion and Shape
concepts.definition: A force can change the speed of a moving object, change its direction, or change its shape.
concepts.key_idea: Force can change how fast an object moves, where it moves, or how it looks.
question_patterns: What are the three main effects of a force?

How can a force change the direction of an object?
How can a force change the shape of an object?

solution_steps.explain: Note the force being applied on the object.
Check whether speed, direction, or shape has changed.
Conclude which of the three effects the force produced.

worked_examples.question: What are the three main effects of a force?
worked_examples.solution: A force can change speed, direction, or shape of an object.

concepts.title: Balanced and Unbalanced Forces
concepts.definition: Balanced forces are equal and opposite forces that do not change motion, while unbalanced forces cause a change in speed or direction.
concepts.key_idea: Unbalanced forces change motion; balanced forces do not.
question_patterns: What are balanced forces?
What are unbalanced forces?
How do balanced and unbalanced forces differ?
Give one example of balanced forces.
Give one example of unbalanced forces.

solution_steps.explain: Check the sizes and directions of the forces acting on the object.
If forces are equal and opposite the net force is zero; otherwise there is a net force.
Balanced forces cause no change in motion; unbalanced forces change motion.

worked_examples.question: What are balanced forces?

worked_examples.answer: Equal and opposite forces with no net effect.

worked_examples.question: What are unbalanced forces?

worked_examples.answer: Forces that cause a change in motion.

concepts.title: Newton's First Law and Inertia
concepts.definition: Newton's first law states that an object stays at rest or in uniform motion unless acted upon by an unbalanced force; this tendency is called inertia.
concepts.key_idea: Objects resist changes to their motion; this resistance is inertia.
question_patterns: What is Newton's first law of motion?
What is inertia?
Why does a passenger fall forward when a bus stops suddenly?
How is inertia related to mass?
Give one example of inertia in daily life.

solution_steps.explain: Note whether the object is at rest or moving uniformly.
See whether an unbalanced force acts on the object.
If no unbalanced force acts, the object keeps its state of motion due to inertia.

worked_examples.question: What is Newton's first law of motion?
worked_examples.solution: An object stays at rest or in uniform motion unless an unbalanced force acts on it.
worked_examples.answer: Objects keep their state of motion unless a force acts.

worked_examples.question: What is inertia?
worked_examples.solution: Inertia is the tendency of an object to resist any change in its state of motion.
worked_examples.answer: The tendency to resist changes in motion.

worked_examples.question: Why does a passenger fall forward when a bus stops suddenly?
worked_examples.solution: The passenger's body tends to keep moving due to inertia when the bus stops.
worked_examples.answer: Inertia keeps the body moving forward.
